sheet-2-1.description: Sheet 2, part 1, is the main map of the north end of Phillipsburg between the Delaware River and North Main Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the lower right. At the top, 2nd Street crosses the sheet beside the Claire Silk Mills, with its weaving shed and warehouse, and the American Horse Shoe Company works stretches along the river bank. The Pennsylvania Railroad's Belvidere Division runs down the centre as a wide band of tracks, with Kroner Place, an arbitrary street, and the Penn R.R. property beside it. North Main Street forms the right side of the map, lined with attached brick and frame dwellings, and 1st Street crosses it near the J. R. Shimer Company pork packers and the Gibney Iron and Steel Company scrap iron yard. The Watson Silk Company mill stands on the left of the tracks. East of North Main Street, Morris Street runs beside a cliff and a stretch of unbuilt hillside, with Chambers Street and Howell Avenue drawn as street lines only. The lower part shows a seed store, a slaughtering house for Chas. Cohen with stock pens, a municipal bath house and other small buildings on the railroad's property, and the Cement Block Works at the very foot. The inset at the lower left, the Tucker and Cameron steam pump works of the Ingersoll-Rand Drill Company, has its own north arrow and is treated as part 2. The compass is at the right of the sheet.
notes: Control is three carried points on the Cement Block Works at the foot of the sheet, also drawn on sheet 4; scale and direction are configured, so the part is low confidence.

North Main Street here is the stretch north of Union Square; no street junction on the sheet could be matched to the modern network, which has been rebuilt as the William Penn Highway and Memorial Parkway.
Kroner Place is printed with the added word Arbitrary.

50 ft; North Main St north of Union Square, Belvidere Division yard, Watson Silk Co, American Horse Shoe; part 1 placed from 3 points carried from sheet 4; part 2 inset (Tucker & Cameron steam pump works) unplaced
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Tucker & Cameron steam pump works (no street junction; needs carried points from a neighbour that draws the works (not found)).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the north end of Phillipsburg, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, between the Delaware River and North Main Street. It runs from 3rd Street across the top to 2nd Street at the foot, with the continuation above on sheet 18 and below on sheet 2. Broad Street runs down the centre of the sheet beside Rose Street and Howell Avenue, which are cut by the alleys named Chintewink, Plott's and Skillman and by Hess Avenue. North Main Street forms the right edge, lined on its west side with closely set frame dwellings and, at the top right, the North End Club and North End Mission. The middle of the sheet is open: a large unbuilt block carries the printed note Base Ball Field, and a steep hillside is marked beyond North Main Street. The left third belongs to industry beside the Pennsylvania Railroad's Belvidere Division tracks: the McNeil Cooperage Company with its stave and barrel storage, and, at the lower left, the buildings of the American Horse Shoe Company (forge shop, scrap iron storage, punching and machine shops, a pump room and a coal pile) down to the Delaware River. Most buildings are coloured yellow for frame, with brick and stone works in red and blue. Water pipes of 4 to 14 inches are drawn in the streets with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Wire Alley, 3rd Street and 2nd Street are drawn as open street lines with few buildings. The scale of feet and the compass are drawn at the foot and top of the sheet; north points to the upper left.
notes: Only 3rd Street, Broad Street and Rose Street survive by name in the modern street network here; Memorial Parkway and the William Penn Highway now occupy the ground to the south and east.
Wire Alley is printed in two parts, WIRE and ALLEY, on either side of Broad.
Placed from the 3rd Street / Broad Street junction at the configured scale and an estimated north direction; low confidence.
50 ft; north end: Broad, Rose, Howell Av, N. Main; anchored on 3rd / Broad only

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the centre of Phillipsburg at Union Square, where the bridge to Easton, Pennsylvania (printed as 595 feet long) reaches the New Jersey bank of the Delaware River. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Along the river the Pennsylvania Railroad's Belvidere Division runs past the passenger station, a long freight house and a baggage and express building, with the Phillipsburg Trust Company, the post office and a bank facing South Main Street. North Main Street leaves the square towards the top, lined with the Hotel Wardell, the Union Square Hotel and a garage, and divides from Morris Street at a long triangle of open ground. Across the top are the Cement Block Works and storage buildings beside the sheet 2 boundary. The right two thirds of the sheet is a residential district of frame dwellings on Washington Street, Harris Street, Bullman Street, Front Street and the curving lanes between them, with a few larger houses set in grounds on the rising ground east of Washington Street. The lower left holds the B.P.O.E. Home and a close grid of small dwellings on Pleasant Avenue, Lake Street and Randall Street, ending at Tyndall Avenue on the lower edge, where sheets 6 and 7 continue. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches and fire hydrants are drawn in most streets. The compass is in the upper left corner and a scale of feet in the lower right.
notes: Control is concentrated in the lower right of the sheet; the Union Square and North Main Street end rests on the fit's extrapolation. The Harris Street / Washington Street fork was left out because the modern lines do not match the drawn ones.
Tyndall Avenue is OpenStreetMap's Tyndall Street west of Front Street and Tyndall Avenue east of it.
The Cement Block Works at the top of the sheet is also drawn at the foot of sheet 2 and was used to carry control to that sheet.
50 ft; Union Square, Washington, Bullman, Harris, Front, B.P.O.E. Home; Harris / Washington fork excluded

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers a residential district of central Phillipsburg east of Washington Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Morris Street crosses the top of the sheet on a long curve, with a few houses and outbuildings on both sides and the sheet 2 boundary above it. Below Morris Street the sheet is ruled into long parallel blocks running from Chambers Street on the left to Fillmore Street on the right: Bennett Street, Bullman Street and Summit Avenue are the cross streets, and narrow alleys named Stull, Burwell and Mitchell run down the middle of each block between them. The blocks are lined with closely set frame dwellings, mostly two storeys with porches, on narrow lots, with small sheds and stables at the rear of the lots on the alleys; a greenhouse stands in the lower left and a few dwellings are of brick or concrete block. Chambers Street runs down the left side and bends where Harris Street meets Bullman Street, and a short row of houses on a triangle between Chambers and Harris Streets fills the lower left corner down to Tyndall Avenue. Dugans Alley, Lewis Street and Sitgreaves Alley are drawn as street lines only along the bottom edge, where sheets 7 and 19 continue. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are marked in the streets. The compass is in the upper right corner and a scale of feet at the foot.
notes: Fillmore Street is spelled Filmore Street in OpenStreetMap.
Stull, Burwell, Mitchell, Dugans and Sitgreaves alleys are not street junctions in the reference data and were not used for control.
50 ft; Morris, Bennett, Bullman, Summit Av between Chambers and Fillmore

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the south end of the centre of Phillipsburg, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with South Main Street running down the middle and the Delaware River and the railroad yards along the left edge. North of Hudson Street the left half is a block of commercial and public buildings between Elizabeth Street, Market Street and South Main Street: the First Presbyterian Church, the City Hall with the Centennial Company, the Eagles Club, a bank at the pointed corner of Market and South Main, a trucking building, and rows of small stores and dwellings. East of South Main Street the blocks run to Brainard Street, with offices, shops, the Sitgreaves Public School and long rows of frame dwellings along Reese Alley. Tyndall Avenue, Stewart Place, Lake Street and Randall Street cut the top right. South of Hudson Street the sheet is mostly railroad: the combined Delaware, Lackawanna and Western and Central Railroad of New Jersey passenger station, the D.L. and W. freight house with its covered platform, the Pennsylvania Railroad's Belvidere Division, the Lehigh Valley passenger station and baggage room, and a spread of yard tracks, bridges over the tracks and a railroad water tank. Hanover Street and Market Street meet at the bottom, with ice houses, a coal shed and storage buildings. The compass is in the upper left and a scale of feet at the foot.
notes: Tyndall Avenue is Tyndall Street west of Front Street and Tyndall Avenue east of it in OpenStreetMap.
Market Street and Elizabeth Street on this sheet survive only as short stubs; the modern nodes at their junctions were not detected and were not used.
The Lehigh Line in the modern rail data lies 11 to 16 m from the drawn Lehigh Valley tracks; no rail control was taken from it.
50 ft; South Main, Hudson, Market, Elizabeth, Hanover, railroad stations; Stryker St dropped

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers a residential district of central Phillipsburg east of Brainard Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Four long north-south streets, Brainard Street on the left, then Washington Street, Chambers Street and Lewis Street, run down the sheet and are crossed at the foot by Hudson Street. Tyndall Avenue runs diagonally across the top left and Summit Avenue across the top right, with Harris Street, Front Street and Shimer Street meeting them. The blocks are lined with closely set frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a few brick houses and rear sheds. Larger features are a range of greenhouses and a blue-coloured house near Tyndall Avenue and Washington Street, two undertaker buildings on Shimer Street, the Westminster Presbyterian Church and the Elshire Apartments on Chambers Street and Lewis Street, and the Chambers Street Theatre (moving pictures) at the corner of Chambers and Hudson. A large open interior block between Washington and Chambers Streets carries lot lines only. Dugans Alley runs down the middle of the Chambers to Lewis block. A retaining wall is drawn along the north side of Tyndall Avenue. Water pipes of 4 and 8 inches and hydrants are shown in the streets. The compass is in the upper right corner and the scale of feet at the lower left. Adjoining sheets are 4 above left, 5 above right, 6 to the left, 9 below left, 10 below and 19 to the right.
notes: Tyndall is lettered without a suffix; it is Tyndall Avenue and Tyndall Street in OpenStreetMap.

Tyndall Avenue and Chambers/Summit junctions at the top of the sheet were not detected; control rests on the Hudson Street junctions along the foot and the Brainard Street junction, so the top is extrapolated (low confidence).
Shimer Street is Shimer Alley in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft; Brainard, Washington, Chambers, Lewis, Hudson, Tyndall Av, Summit Av (diagonals left out)

sheet-8-1.description: Sheet 8, part 1, is the main map of the sheet and covers the south end of Phillipsburg's business district and the Lehigh Valley railroad yard, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. South Main Street runs from the top right corner down the right side of the sheet, bending at Mercer Street and continuing south to River Street. At the top Hanover Street and Market Street enclose a block holding the Cedar Auditorium, the Phillipsburg Hotel and rows of frame dwellings, and Reese Court runs through the block below it, lined with brick and frame dwellings and the premises of Rhodes Brothers, dealers in electrical and automobile supplies. Mercer Street and, to the south, West Mercer Street run diagonally between the yard and South Main Street, with long rows of attached dwellings, a garage, the John H. Hagerty lumber company, the Thomas Newman's Sons coal yard with its coal pockets, the Public Library and the First Baptist Church near River Street. The left half is the Lehigh Valley Railroad yard: dozens of parallel tracks, the L.V.R.R. freight house and its offices, a signal tower, a motor repair shop and a stretch of the Pennsylvania Railroad Belvidere Division on the high bluff at the far left. A heavy-lined inset of the Lehigh Valley repair shops occupies the left edge and is treated as part 2; below it a turntable and a few small buildings are drawn. The compass is at the right and a scale of feet at the foot.
notes: West Mercer Street and the Mercer Street continuation are Mercer Street in OpenStreetMap.

Only the Hanover Street / South Main Street, Hanover Street / Market Street and Market Street / Reese Court junctions were detected; the Mercer Street junctions did not match the drawn street lines. The fit uses three points and is low confidence.
The inset of the Lehigh Valley repair shops at the lower left is excluded from this part's mask.
50 ft; Hanover, Reese Ct, Mercer, S. Main, River, Lehigh Valley yard; part 2 inset (Lehigh Valley RR repair shops) unplaced
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Lehigh Valley RR repair shops (no street junction; needs carried points from sheet 9 or 11 (not found)).

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the Central Railroad of New Jersey yards and shops in the heart of Phillipsburg, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the street grid runs diagonally across the page. Most of the sheet is occupied by a wide fan of tracks of the Central R.R. of N.J., with the D.L. & W. R.R. (Morris & Essex Division) lines along the east side. At the centre stand the ten-stall roundhouse and turntable, with the machine shop, blacksmith shop, engine house, supplies and oil houses and a water tank beside them; a long freight platform and a signal tower lie to the north. On the west side the yard is bounded by South Main Street, which runs from the upper centre down the left edge. Along it are Swift & Co. meat packers, a monument works, a Central R.R. of N.J. freight house with its platform, the First M.E. Church, and the John H. Hagerty lumber company with its sheds at the foot, beside Cross Street. Hanover Street enters South Main from the west at the top left, with a steel bridge over the railroad tracks beyond it, and Reese Court and Mercer Street meet it at the left edge. On the east side a short row of frame dwellings and a carriage shop line Brainard Street and Hudson Street at the top right, and Washington Street runs up the right edge with rows of dwellings, meeting Hudson Street at the middle right. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches and fire hydrants are drawn along the streets. The compass is at the upper right, and the sheet is bordered by sheets 6, 7, 8, 10 and 13.
notes: The part is placed from three detected junctions (Hanover Street / South Main Street, Brainard Street / Hudson Street, Cross Street / South Main Street) and one hand-picked point (Hudson Street / Washington Street); few junctions survive in the rail yard, so confidence is medium.
Mercer Street / South Main Street, at the left edge, could not be read on the sheet and was not used.
Centre Avenue and Shimer Street are not in the reference data and were not used for control.
50 ft; S Main, Hudson, Brainard, Hanover, Cross; CRR of NJ yard and roundhouse

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers a residential district of central Phillipsburg drawn at 50 feet to an inch, east of Washington Street. The part runs from Hudson Street at the top to Ellen Street at the bottom, crossed midway by Fulton Street, and from Washington Street on the left to Fillmore on the right, with Chambers Street and Lewis Street between. Narrow alleys run down the middle of the long blocks: Taylor Alley between Washington and Chambers, Dugans Alley between Chambers and Lewis, and Sitgreaves Alley between Lewis and Fillmore. Beyond Fillmore the sheet shows only the street lines of Irwin Street and Bowhay Avenue, which belong to sheet 19. The blocks are lined with closely spaced frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a few brick houses and small stores, sheds and stables at the rear of the lots. Notable buildings are the Wesley M.E. Church on Lewis Street, the firehouse of the Alert Hook and Ladder Company No. 6 on Chambers Street, the Fifth Ward Hotel on Chambers Street below Fulton, and a brick building with a hall at the corner of Hudson and Fillmore. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are drawn along most streets, with fire hydrants. The lower left of the sheet, below Fulton Street and west of Chambers Street, is left blank except for outlines; it is drawn on sheet 13. Adjoining sheets are 7 above, 9 to the left, 13 below left and 19 to the right. A scale of feet and the compass are drawn in the blank lower left corner.
notes: Fillmore Street is spelled Filmore Street in OpenStreetMap.
Taylor, Dugans and Sitgreaves alleys are not in the reference data as streets and were not used for control.
50 ft; pilot. Hudson, Fulton, Ellen, Washington, Chambers, Lewis, Fillmore (OSM Filmore Street); alleys Taylor, Dugans, Sitgreaves

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the west edge of Phillipsburg between the Delaware River and Howard Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run diagonally across the page. The left two thirds of the sheet is taken up by the Pennsylvania Railroad's Belvidere Division yard, a broad fan of tracks labelled the Penna. R.R. Freight Yard, with the P.R.R. main lines along the Delaware River at the left edge. Between them runs the Morris Canal, drawn in blue. On the canal bank stand the Port Delaware Boat Building and Repair Shops of the Morris Canal, property of the Lehigh Valley R.R. and noted as not operated, with a wood working shop, an open shed for wagons and patterns, and a blacksmith shop; a bunk house, an office with a supply room, and the P.R.R. car shops with a wash house, blacksmith shop and lumber shed lie further east and south. Along the right side is a residential district of closely built frame dwellings on narrow lots, between Howard Street and Fayette Street. Carling Street, Fox Street and Stockton Street cross Howard Street from the top to the bottom of the sheet, with Chestnut Alley running between Howard and Fayette. Lehigh Street is drawn at the top, and a few street lines show at the top right where the sheet meets sheet 8. The compass and the scale of feet are drawn in the blank yard area. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along Chestnut Alley, Stockton Street and the top. Adjoining sheets are 8 above, 12 to the right and 14 below.
notes: Only one street junction on the sheet (Howard Street / Stockton Street) is in the reference data; the part is anchored on it with the atlas scale, so its rotation and scale rest on one point and its confidence is low.

Carling Street, Fayette Street, Lehigh Street and Chestnut Alley are not in the reference data under these names, and the modern Fox Street is a short street elsewhere; the Fox Street drawn here is not used for control.
The Delaware River label is cut by the left edge of the sheet; the first letters are not visible.
50 ft; Howard, Carling, Fox, Fayette, Stockton, Lehigh St; PRR yard, Morris Canal; anchored on Howard / Stockton

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers a dense part of central Phillipsburg on the slope above the Delaware, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run diagonally across the page. The part runs from River Street at the top down to Stockton Street at the bottom, and from the Lehigh Valley R.R. tracks at the left edge to Sitgreaves Street on the right. Between them, Cherry Alley, Mercer Street, Cedar Alley, South Main Street and Spruce Alley run down the page, crossed by Fox Street and Jersey Street. The blocks hold closely built frame dwellings on narrow lots, with stores along South Main Street, among them the Tuxedo moving pictures, a club and a bakery, and the B.P.O.E. hall and printing office on the blocks below. The principal institutions are the Lovell School and the High School with its manual training building, in the upper right between South Main and Sitgreaves Streets, and the St. Philip and St. James R.C. Church with its rectory at the foot of South Main Street. Lumber sheds of the formerly J.H. Hagerty Lumber Co., marked to be removed, stand on River Street, and the J.E. Fleming coal pockets lie in the upper left corner beside the railroad. Several garages and a Ford sales and service building are shown. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches run along River, West Mercer and Stockton Streets and South Main Street. The compass is at the top centre. Sheet 8 lies above, 13 to the right and 15 below.
notes: Placed from eight detected street junctions at RMSE 1.3 m (leave-one-out 2.5 m); Cherry, Cedar and Spruce alleys and West Mercer Street are not in the reference data as streets and were not used for control.
50 ft; River, Mercer, Fox, S Main, Jersey, Sitgreaves, Stockton

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 lies across the Central Railroad of New Jersey and Delaware, Lackawanna & Western tracks in central Phillipsburg, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run diagonally across the page. A broad band of railroad yard tracks, with a coal elevator, tipples, a reinforced concrete coal dock and a high embankment, divides two built-up strips. On the west side, Sitgreaves Street runs from Cross Street at the top, past Jersey Street, down to Stockton Street at the bottom, lined with frame dwellings, a dyeing and key cleaning shop, the Phillipsburg Supply & Construction Co. office and, at the centre, the John H. Hagerty Lumber Co. planing mill with its lumber piles and frame and bench work departments. Pine Alley runs behind the lower Sitgreaves blocks. On the east side, Washington Street, Taylor Alley and Chambers Street run down from Fulton Street across rows of narrow dwelling lots, with St. John's Evangelical Lutheran Church and its rectory on Fulton Street and the Reliance Hose Company No. 3 fire department building on Taylor Alley. Washington Street turns diagonally below the middle of the sheet toward Chambers Street, with Hill, marked private, below it and the Eagle Hotel at the lower right. Heckman Street and Ellen Street join Chambers Street at the right edge, and Stockton Street crosses the sheet at the bottom, passing under overhead steel bridges. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches follow most streets. The compass is at the lower left, with sheet 12 beside it. Adjoining sheets are 8 and 9 at the top left, 10 above the right strip, 19 to the right and 15 and 24 below.
notes: Placed from eight detected junctions (RMSE 1.5 m, leave-one-out 2.3 m); Chambers Street / Washington Street, where Washington Street runs in diagonally, has the largest residual (3.1 m).
Taylor Alley, Pine Alley and Hill (marked private on the sheet) are not in the reference data as streets and were not used for control.
The modern Lehigh Line lies about 16 m from the railroad drawn here, so rail crossings were not used.
50 ft; Sitgreaves, Cross, Jersey, Washington, Fulton, Chambers, Heckman, Stockton; rail yard

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows the west side of Phillipsburg along the Delaware River and the Morris Canal, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run diagonally across the page. The left half is taken up by railroad and industrial land. The Pennsylvania R.R. Belvidere Division tracks run down beside the canal, with the Pennsylvania R.R. locomotive house and its turntable near the top, a machine shop with pumps, storage and offices, an oil house and a water tank below it. Below them stands the large plant of the Tippet & Wood Boiler & Tank Works, a long group of boiler shops, machine shop, pattern shop and rivet storage, with a wagon shed, offices, a storage yard, a print shop and a signal tower around it. The right half is a residential district between Howard Street and the Lehigh Valley R.R. tracks at the right edge. Stockton Street runs across the top and Jefferson Street crosses the middle, with Howard Street, Chestnut Alley, Fayette Street and Cherry Alley running down the page between them. Closely spaced frame dwellings on narrow lots line Howard Street and Fayette Street above Jefferson Street, while the blocks below are largely empty apart from a few houses. A steel overhead bridge carries a street across the railroad tracks at the right edge, near the junction of Jefferson Street and Cherry Alley. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along Stockton Street, Chestnut Alley and Howard Street. The compass is at the lower left. Adjoining sheets are 11 above, 15 to the right and 16 below.
notes: Only one street junction (Howard Street / Stockton Street) is in the reference data; the part is anchored on it with the atlas scale, so its rotation and scale rest on one point and its confidence is low.
Jefferson Street, Fayette Street, Chestnut Alley and Cherry Alley as drawn here do not meet other modern streets at junctions that could be used as control.
50 ft; Howard, Jefferson, Fayette, Stockton; PRR locomotive house; points carried from sheet 15 (steel overhead bridge)

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 is a dense residential and commercial part of central Phillipsburg between Stockton Street at the top and the Warren Foundry area at the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run diagonally across the page. Jefferson Street crosses the middle of the sheet, and Mercer Street, South Main Street and Sitgreaves Street run down it, with Cherry Alley, Cedar Alley and Spruce Alley between them. Fayette Street is lettered at the left edge, beside the Lehigh Valley R.R. tracks, which pass under a steel overhead bridge at the left. The blocks are packed with frame and brick dwellings on narrow lots and stores along South Main Street. Notable buildings include the St. Philip and St. James Parochial School at the top of the block between Mercer and South Main Streets, Grace Evangelical Church with a parsonage and a battery service station, the Lehigh Furniture Co. (wholesale), M.J. Cannon coal and wood yard, a garage with capacity for 35 cars, St. Catherine's Convent of Mercy, a bakery and an auto repair shop. At the right edge lies the power plant of the Warren Foundry & Pipe Co., with its engine room, condensers and a coal pile, above a block of dwellings. Water pipes of 6 to 10 inches follow Stockton Street, Mercer Street and Sitgreaves Street. The compass is at the upper left. Adjoining sheets are 12 above, 14 to the left, 16 below and 24 to the right.
notes: Placed from six detected junctions at RMSE 0.5 m (leave-one-out 1.0 m); high confidence.
The fitted scale is 7.99 px/ft, about 1.4 percent above the atlas value of 7.88.
McKeen Street, at the foot of the sheet, centres 90 to 100 ft off the sheet and was not measured.
50 ft; Stockton, Jefferson, Mercer, S Main, Sitgreaves

sheet-16-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 16 is the main map of the southern edge of central Phillipsburg, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run diagonally across the page. McKeen Street crosses the top. Below it Mercer Street, South Main Street and Sitgreaves Street run down the page, with Cherry Alley at the far left, Cedar Alley between Mercer and South Main Streets and Spruce Alley between South Main and Sitgreaves Streets. Smith Avenue crosses the middle and Abbett Street the foot of the sheet. Mercer Street swings south-eastward below the middle of the sheet to join South Main Street, passing the Lehigh Valley R.R. tracks and a long stretch marked no exposure. The blocks along South Main Street and Sitgreaves Street are densely built with frame dwellings, stores and a few brick buildings. Institutions include the L.O. Beers Public School between Mercer and South Main Streets, the Jersey Hose Company No. 2 with its hose tower, a bottling works, St. Luke's Episcopal Church with its parish hall and rectory, and, at the lower right, storage lumber and contractors' supplies and Kopp & Kopp contractors' ware house and private garage. A steel bridge carries a street over the railroad at the upper left. Blocks west of Mercer Street are largely empty, with scattered dwellings. The lower left corner of the sheet is the inset drawn as part 2, set apart by a heavy line. The compass is at the left centre. Adjoining sheets are 15 above, 24 to the right and 17 below.
notes: Placed from eight detected junctions (RMSE 0.7 m, leave-one-out 1.3 m); high confidence.
Abbett Street is Abbott Street at South Main Street and Abbet Street at Sitgreaves Street in the reference data (one street with two spellings).
Cherry Alley, Cedar Alley and Spruce Alley are not in the reference data as streets and were not used for control.
50 ft; part 1 McKeen, Mercer, S Main, Smith Av, Sitgreaves, Abbett; part 2 inset (Howard, McKeen, Fayette) anchored on a hand pick

sheet-16-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 16 is an inset at the lower left corner, set off from the main map by a heavy line and covering the south-west end of the area shown on sheet 14. It shows the end of Howard Street, with Chestnut Alley, Fayette Street and McKeen Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Howard Street runs down the left edge to McKeen Street, which crosses the inset from left to right and ends at a steel bridge over the Lehigh Valley R.R. tracks at the right. Chestnut Alley and Fayette Street run up from McKeen Street, and Mount Fayette, as the lower road is lettered, runs down from it. Frame dwellings stand on the north side of Howard Street and Chestnut Alley, and a row of four dwellings, numbers 8, 10, 12 and 14, lies along the south side of McKeen Street; a few more houses stand further south. Most of the inset is blank land, marked as an area to be taken over for a railroad yard, with the block numbers 82, 99 and 100. The frame of the inset is lettered no exposure. A separate compass is drawn in the blank lower part. The main map of the sheet lies above and to the right.
notes: Anchored on one hand-picked point (Howard Street / McKeen Street) with the atlas scale and the rotation of the neighbouring sheets; low confidence. The west side of Howard Street is cut by the edge of the inset, so the junction was taken midway between the drawn edges.
Fayette Street is not in the reference data and was not used for control.
50 ft; part 1 McKeen, Mercer, S Main, Smith Av, Sitgreaves, Abbett; part 2 inset (Howard, McKeen, Fayette) anchored on a hand pick

sheet-17-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 17 is the left-hand strip of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 65 degrees from the page, covering the south end of Phillipsburg along South Main Street. A heavy vertical line on the right divides it from part 2, the chemical works and rail yards. South Main Street runs down the strip beside the Morris Canal, which is drawn as a double blue band along the left edge. At the top Abbett Street and Sitgreaves Street bound the large Korp Coal Company block, with its coal pocket inclined from the bank to street level and a railroad branch of several tracks running through a tunnel at Center Street. Center Street crosses below the coal yard, with a filling station, a row of frame dwellings and a cluster of buildings at its junction with Andover Street. Down the strip the east side of South Main Street is lined with houses numbered about 676 to 771 and the Andover Hotel, with the Greek Catholic Church (Slavish) at the middle of block 107. Andover Street runs south into Limekiln Road, which swings away south-east along a steep cliff above the lots numbered 747 to 771. The Bruch Public School stands at the upper left across the canal. East of Andover Street the block marked 107A has houses along Limekiln Road and a railroad storage shed and ruins of a fire beside the heavy line, where the note No Exposure is lettered. The sheet is continued on sheets 16, 24, 27 and 28, and a scale of feet is drawn at the foot.
notes: Abbett Street is Abbet Street in OpenStreetMap; its junction with South Main Street (Abbott Street) was used as a boundary point.
The canal lettering reads Morri and Canal and is cut by the sheet edge; the name Morris Canal is inferred.
Placed from five points, two of them hand picked (Andover Street / Limekiln Road and Limekiln Road / South Main Street at the cliff), because few junctions were detected; medium confidence.
50 ft; two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 S. Main, Center, Andover, Limekiln Rd; part 2 Thompson chemical works and yards (unplaced)
Not georeferenced on this sheet: Thompson chemical works and rail yards, Broad St (no street junction; needs carried points from sheet 18 part 1 (step 6b)).

sheet-18-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 18 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 36 degrees from the page. It shows the north end of Phillipsburg between the Delaware River and the high ground above North Main Street. A heavy line at the upper left separates it from part 2. A pair of parallel streets, Broad and Rose, run north-east across the top, crossed by 3rd and 4th streets and by Chintewink Alley and Andrews Alley, with blocks numbered 1, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, 5 and 6. North Main Street runs along the heavy line and then curves south-east below a steep, unbuilt hillside lettered Cliff, Top of Hill and Steep. The blocks along Broad and Rose are closely built with frame dwellings, and the Schedler Murphy Iron and Steel Corporation, dealers in scrap iron, occupies the top. The Mandarin Silk Corporation mill stands on 3rd Street, the Alliance Holt Dye Works and Howell School on Davis Court and Fairview Avenue, and the Breen Silk Company near Opitz Avenue. The lower left is a regular grid of narrow lots between Fillmore, Raymond and Summit Avenue, crossed by Bennett, Bullman, Schaffer Avenue, Burwell Alley, Mitchell Alley, Orchard Alley and Morris, with Joseph Street and the Cedar Park Hotel to the east. The right edge is mostly unbuilt, with Meadow Avenue, an electric railroad right of way and a range of woods. Adjoining sheets are 32 above, 305 right, 5, 6, 7 and 11 left, 19 below.
notes: Fillmore is lettered Fillmore here (Filmore Street in OpenStreetMap).
Summit Avenue and the Broad, Rose, 3rd and 4th street junctions of the modern network lie 4 to 6 m off their drawn lines and were not used as control.
The part above the heavy line at the upper left (Broad, Rose, Chintewink Alley, Judd Alley and North Alley west of the line, with the compass marked 7) is a separate part and is not georeferenced.

100 ft; part 1 north end (Broad, Rose, Morris, Fairview, Belvidere Av ...); part 2 above the heavy line top left (west Broad, Rose, alleys) unplaced; Summit Av and Broad/Rose at 3rd/4th left out as displaced
Not georeferenced on this sheet: area above the heavy line top left: west Broad, Rose, alleys (no junction of two surviving streets; needs carried points from sheet 17 part 1 or 18 part 1).

sheet-19-1.description: Sheet 19, main part, shows the north-eastern residential district of Phillipsburg drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned about 36 degrees from the page. Summit Avenue and Green Alley cross the top; Glen Avenue, Hudson and Irwin run down the sheet between them, cut by Evelyn Avenue, Schultz Avenue, Henshaw Court, Francis and Miller streets. On the left the grid gives way to a diagonal pair of streets, Lewis and Fillmore, with Sitgreaves Alley between the older lots near Hudson Street, where the Freeman Public School stands. The upper half is rows of narrow frame dwellings with small outbuildings, a bake house, a plumber's shop and a few stores. In the middle of the sheet Irwin Street borders the large Phillipsburg Cemetery and the Catholic Cemetery, which are left blank except for outlines and the lot lines of the cemetery, and a large garage with a capacity of 80 cars stands at Irwin and Fillmore. The lower half returns to dense blocks of dwellings on Bowhay Avenue, John, Mary, Davis, Colby Place, Heckman, Silk, Stockton and Railroad Avenue, with the Jerico Silk Company and a foundry among them. Lewis Street runs south-east past Dugan's Alley, Ellen and Chambers streets to Madison Square. The lower left corner is cut off by a heavy line; the Stockton, Warren and Firth streets beyond it form part 2 of this sheet. Water pipes with fire hydrants are drawn along most streets. Adjoining sheets are 5 and 7 on the left and top, 18 above, 21 to the right of the cemetery, 13 below left and 24 and 10 below.
notes: Fillmore is spelled Filmore Street in OpenStreetMap. Summit Avenue, near Fillmore and Schultz, lies several metres off its drawn line and was left out of the control.
Irwin Street junctions with Evelyn and Schultz avenues were 5 to 6 m off the drawn line and Irwin Street was left out of the control.
Lewis Street is the modern Lewis Street; Fulton Street, drawn at the cemetery, survives as Fulton Street.
100 ft; part 1 Summit, Glen Av, Hudson, Lewis, Davis, Heckman, Stockton, Phillipsburg Cemetery (Irwin left out); part 2 lower left turned 67 deg (Firth, Warren, Stockton, Anderson) anchored

sheet-19-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 19 is a detached piece in the lower left corner, bounded by a heavy line on its right and above, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 67 degrees from the page, with its own north arrow. It shows the north end of the Warren and Firth street area of Phillipsburg, which is the ground that sheet 21 draws in full. Firth and Warren streets run up the part from the lower left to Stockton Street at the top, where a short stretch of Stockton Street crosses them. Anderson Street runs across the bottom of the part, and a dashed water pipe in Warren Street continues down to it. Both streets are lined by short rows of narrow frame dwellings along the east side of Firth Street and the west side of Warren Street, with houses numbered 401 to 417 and 427 to 446. Larger works stand near Anderson Street: the Tirrell Bros. Silk Corporation, with a pier construction building on open steel, at the lower left, and the Gunning Silk Company, a weaving and winding plant, with the Pennsylvania Power Company substation beside it at the lower right. Much of the part is blank ground between the blocks. The scale of 100 feet is printed at the foot, with the note No Exposure along the lower edge. Block numbers 24, 66, 67, 68 and 399 are printed in the part, and it is continued on sheets 21, 24 and 13.
notes: Placed from two junctions that the detector measured (Stockton / Warren and Firth / Stockton, 82 m apart), so scale comes from the configuration; low confidence.
100 ft; part 1 Summit, Glen Av, Hudson, Lewis, Davis, Heckman, Stockton, Phillipsburg Cemetery (Irwin left out); part 2 lower left turned 67 deg (Firth, Warren, Stockton, Anderson) anchored

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers Delaware Park and Hillcrest, a suburban district in Lopatcong Township east of Phillipsburg, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 36 degrees from the page. The title box gives the population as 500, with a volunteer fire department of 40 men, a one-chief 40-gallon chemical engine and 1500 feet of hose, public lighting by electricity and streets not paved. The streets form a loose grid: Beers, Prospect, Park Avenue, Aurora and Belvidere Avenue cross the sheet, cut by 1st, 2nd and 3rd streets, with the alleys Vine, Chestnut, Oak, Fortuna and Venus between the blocks. Most of the blocks are large, mapped as numbered lots with only a scattering of frame dwellings and outbuildings, and the blocks around The Park, in the middle of the sheet, are left almost empty. Buildings of note are the Delaware Park Public School on Aurora Street, the Delaware Park Mission, the Abel E. Merritt Silk Company and Delaware Park Chemical Engine Company on 1st Street, and a club with a ball field and grand stand at the left. The lower third of the sheet shows the planned curving streets of Hillcrest: Fairbanks, Ferguson, Barrymore, Lincoln, Clarke, Burke and Harte streets and Hillcrest Boulevard, laid out around numbered lots 502 to 512 with very few houses. The township boundary of Lopatcong runs along the left and bottom edges. Adjoining sheets are 21 and 22 to the south, 302 to 304 at the top and 19 to the west.
notes: Streets are printed with the lettering 1st, 2nd and 3rd Street; the modern names are North 1st, North 2nd and North 3rd Street.
Clarke Street appears to be today's Liner Boulevard, and the curving 2nd Street south of Belvidere Avenue appears to be Hagerty Avenue (inferred from the fit).
Hillcrest Boulevard, Fairbanks and the other curving Hillcrest streets were laid out but mostly unbuilt in 1925.
The lettering at the top left, read as Lower Belvidere Rd., is partly cut off by the sheet edge.
100 ft; Delaware Park: Beers, Prospect, Park Av, Aurora, Belvidere Av, 1st-3rd St, Hillcrest Blvd

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers the eastern residential district of Phillipsburg and the northern edge of the Hillcrest development, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 36 degrees from the page. The lower two thirds is a regular grid of long narrow blocks between Railroad Avenue on the left and Bates Street on the right, crossed by Marshall at the middle and Heckman and Stockton at the foot, with Wilson, Firth, Warren, Grant, Lincoln and Prospect streets running down the sheet and Tighe's Alley between Railroad Avenue and Wilson. Blocks are lined with frame dwellings, many in attached rows, and the sheet shows the Italian American Club, the Syrian Roman Catholic Church, the Prospect Street Union Mission, the Lincoln Engine Company No. 5, a bakery and the John Firth Public School on Prospect Street. Above Marshall Street the blocks thin out into large unbuilt lots. The upper third is the curving layout of Hillcrest: Hillcrest Boulevard, Potts Avenue, Warner, Reese, Morris, Corliss Avenue, Hudson, Irwin, Henderson, Miller and Francis streets frame numbered lots 518 to 544, with a few houses and a filling station on Potts Avenue and the Hillcrest Apartments, a row of attached brick apartment buildings, near the top left. A garage for 10 cars stands at Morris and Lincoln. At the right edge only street lines are drawn for Grace, Engine, Drill, Elder, Compressor and Ingersoll streets, which belong to sheet 22. The compass is drawn in the open block west of Lincoln Street. Adjoining sheets are 19 above and to the left, 24 below the left and 22 on the right.
notes: Firth Street is lettered Firth (Teel).
Grace Avenue, Engine Street, Drill Street, Elder Avenue and Compressor Street at the right edge are street lines only; they are drawn in full on sheet 22.
Stockton / Warren and Corliss Avenue / Warren Street junctions of the modern network did not match the drawn streets and were not used for control.
100 ft; Hillcrest: Corliss, Grace, Elder, Lincoln, Warren, Marshall, Bates, Heckman; Hudson, Miller, Warren north of Marshall rejected as displaced

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 shows the Hillcrest district on the south-eastern edge of Phillipsburg, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Hillcrest Boulevard curves across the top of the sheet, with Burke, Harte and Pickford Avenue running south from it and Barrymore crossing them below. Pickford Avenue is the main street of the sheet and runs south-south-west past John Mitchell Avenue to the lower edge, while Frederick, 3rd Street and Metz Avenue are drawn as street lines on the right. A dash-dot line crossing the sheet below Barrymore is the boundary between Lopatcong Township and the Town of Phillipsburg. Above it, at the top, the land is mostly large unbuilt blocks numbered 513 to 516, with a few dwellings along Hillcrest Boulevard and Pickford Avenue and a cluster of houses on the curved streets at upper right. Below the boundary a grid of long, narrow blocks lies between Willever, Frace, Ingersoll, Sargeant and Pickford, cut by John Mitchell, Grace, Engine, Drill, Corliss and Elder Avenues, with small frame dwellings along the streets. The lower left holds the Rainbow Silk Manufacturing Company plant on Elder Avenue, with a pier-construction building and curtain walls, and a garage near Morris Street. The right and lower right of the sheet are largely blank blocks, numbered 526 to 538, and a road marked not opened runs south through block 395. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches are shown on several streets, with hydrants. The compass at upper left points up and to the left. Adjoining sheets are 20 above and 21 to the left.
notes: Sargeant Avenue is Sargent Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The street lettered Rand Avenue continues the line of Pickford Avenue south of Elder Avenue; it was not used for control (modern Rand Boulevard is a different road).
Frederick Street in OpenStreetMap runs a block west of the street drawn as Frederick on this sheet and was not used for control.
100 ft; Hillcrest east: Pickford, John Mitchell Av, Grace, Corliss, Elder, Sargeant (= Sargent Avenue); Frederick St left out (modern line a block off)

sheet-23-1.description: Sheet 23 part 1 is the village of Morris Park, in Lopatcong Township east of Phillipsburg, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. A grid of streets runs down the sheet: 1st to 7th Streets from left to right, crossed by Dana, Cromwell and Baltimore Streets, with Morris Turnpike cutting diagonally along the bottom edge. Edward Street, marked not opened, appears at the upper left. The upper third of the sheet is mostly numbered but unbuilt blocks (319 to 328) with a handful of dwellings and outbuildings. Building is concentrated in the middle and lower blocks (329 to 341), where long rows of narrow numbered lots are laid out between the streets, most still without houses. The Morris Park School stands on Cromwell Street at 2nd Street and the Kilton Brothers Silk Mill, a brick works with a cement floor on iron piers, stands near 4th and 5th Streets below Baltimore Street, with hen houses nearby. Small frame dwellings with sheds line Morris Turnpike at the bottom. A legend at upper right gives the population of Morris Park as 300, the turnpike as concrete paved with public lights electric, water facilities as poor and fire department as none. A boxed area at the top right, with its own north arrow, shows Morris Turnpike again at another orientation and is a separate part, not included here. The compass at top centre points up and slightly left. The main street grid is turned about 17 degrees from the sheet edges.
notes: The numbered streets are South 1st to South 7th Street in OpenStreetMap; the other streets keep their names.
Edward Street is marked not opened on the sheet and was not used for control.

Morris Turnpike is not used for control: the modern road along the bottom edge is Memorial Parkway, and the Washington Secondary railroad lies about 28 m from the line the sheet draws, so railroad crossings were turned off.
100 ft; Morris Park: 1st-7th St (= South 1st-7th Street), Edward, Dana, Cromwell, Baltimore; part 2 box top right (Morris Turnpike) unplaced
Not georeferenced on this sheet: box top right: Morris Turnpike (no street junction; needs a parcel corner).

sheet-24-1.description: Sheet 24 part 1 covers the industrial district along the railroads on the south-east side of Phillipsburg, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies toward the upper right. A broad belt of Lehigh Valley and Delaware, Lackawanna and Western tracks runs down the middle of the sheet, with a roundhouse and turntable of the D.L. and W.R.R. locomotive house at the top. At the left, between the tracks and the sheet edge, are the works of the Warren Foundry and Pipe Company: pipe foundries, a clay mill, machine shop, pipe cooling sheds, tar dipping and testing houses, a locomotive house and a pipe storage yard, along Sitgreaves Street and McKeen Street. The Phillipsburg Supply and Construction Company's lumber and building materials yard lies beside the tracks at the top centre. At upper right is the large Standard Silk Company plant, with weave sheds, a cloth room, boiler house and storage buildings, on Stockton Street. Railroad Avenue, Wilson and Firth Streets are laid out south-west of Stockton Street as long empty blocks, numbered 65 and 65A, closed at their lower end by Anderson Street, with a few dwellings along Firth. A road named Constantia curves across the lower centre past a line of small dwellings and sheds. A notice inside the Standard Silk plant records that admittance is refused and that the plan is from an old map, partly verified. The Warren Foundry and Pipe Company box at lower right is a separate part. Adjoining sheets are 13 above left, 15 and 16 at the left, 19 and 21 at the right and 17 below.
notes: Anderson is drawn on the line of modern Fleming Drive in OpenStreetMap, which is the name used for control.
Silk Street is Silk Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

Control rests on six points in the north-east corner (Stockton Street, Wilson, Firth and Fleming Drive); the railroad yard at the left is placed by extension of that fit and agrees with the modern Lehigh Line and Washington Secondary tracks.
100 ft; rail yard, Standard Silk Co, Warren Foundry; part 1 Stockton, Silk, Railroad Av, Wilson, Firth, Anderson (= Fleming Drive); part 2 box lower right (Sitgreaves / Abbett) anchored

sheet-24-2.description: Sheet 24 part 2 is a boxed detail at the lower right of the sheet, set off by heavy lines and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the same north-east orientation as the main map. It shows the Warren Foundry and Pipe Company works between Sitgreaves Street and the railroad tracks: a long pattern shop and green sand foundry, a storage building, boiler or steam rooms, and a row of small dwellings or offices, numbered 34 to 52, beside the tracks. Abbett Street runs in from the left to Sitgreaves Street, with a six-inch water pipe along it, and Spruce Alley lies to the left of the works. Center Street crosses the bottom of the box diagonally, passing over a steel bridge and retaining wall at the tracks, and a tunnel is marked at the lower left near block 105. The railroad tracks of the Lehigh and Delaware, Lackawanna and Western lines fill the right half of the box, with a note that the ground is not exposed at the right edge. Blocks 104, 105 and 107A are numbered. The compass at the top of the box points toward the upper right.
notes: Abbett Street is spelled Abbet Street in OpenStreetMap.

Placed from one street junction (Abbet Street and Sitgreaves Street) with the scale of the main part and a rotation measured from its own lines, which agrees with the main part to 2.7 degrees; low confidence.
100 ft; rail yard, Standard Silk Co, Warren Foundry; part 1 Stockton, Silk, Railroad Av, Wilson, Firth, Anderson (= Fleming Drive); part 2 box lower right (Sitgreaves / Abbett) anchored

sheet-25-1.description: Sheet 25 part 1 is the Lopatcong and Phillipsburg district around Center Street at the south-eastern edge of the town, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 36 degrees, so that north points toward the upper right. Center Street crosses the sheet as the horizontal street at mid height. Below it a regular grid of numbered blocks (119 to 132) lies between Sayre Avenue, Wilbur Avenue, Columbus Avenue and Green Street, cut by Thomas, Ann, James and Pursel Streets, with small lettered alleys between the lots. Most lots are narrow and carry single frame dwellings with sheds, with some stores along Center Street, a garage and larger buildings near Thomas Street and Columbus Avenue, and the Keystone Hotel on Thomas Street at the right. The St. Peter and St. Paul Slovak church (Roman Catholic) with its school stands at the left on Sayre Avenue. Above Center Street the blocks are long, empty strips (117 and 118) running back from the street, closed by an abandoned quarry shown beyond, with Warren Street and a private way at the upper left leading to the Reynolds Silk Company works, which weave, wind and warp silk in a large pink-coloured brick mill. A note at the right edge reads Cameron Pump Works beyond. Two boxed details at the top, one of Center Street at Sayre Avenue with the Wallace Silk Company and one of Center Street at Roseberry Street, have their own north arrows and are separate parts. A railroad crosses the top of the sheet. Adjoining sheets are 27 below left and 28 below.
notes: Warren is Warren Street and Sayre Avenue is Sayre Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Center is Center Street.
The bottom row Pursel Street lies on the sheet edge; its junction with Wilbur Avenue carries a residual of 3.6 m.
100 ft; Center, Thomas, Ann, James, Pursel, Warren, Sayre, Wilbur, Columbus, Green; parts 2 (Wallace Silk Co, Center / Sayre Av) and 3 (Roseberry (Center)) boxes at top unplaced
Not georeferenced on this sheet: box at top: Center Street at Sayre Av, Wallace Silk Co (detector found nothing; Sayre node at the box edge; needs hand-picked points).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: box top right: Roseberry (Center) / Center (Roseberry is Center changing its name, not a junction; needs hand-picked points or a parcel corner).

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers the south-eastern edge of Phillipsburg between the Morris Canal and the railroad on the west and the Lopatcong grid on the east, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 36 degrees, so that north points toward the upper right. In the upper left, South Main Street runs down the sheet beside the tracks, with Pursel Street joining it at the top and a group of dwellings, a hall and an extract works, with a pump house and sewage basins, along it. The canal and the river bank wind through the lower left, where the Rock Products Company soapstone mill and a mill with a boiler stand on the canal at the bottom and the compass is drawn in blank paper. The railroad tracks of the Lehigh Valley run in a belt down the middle of the sheet, with Bank Street beside them. To the right is a grid of long numbered blocks (345, 346, 139, 143 to 149) between Hill Street, Wilbur Avenue and Mill Street, crossed by Congress Street and, in the lower half, by Steel Street and Kent Street, where the grid bends and the blocks run at a different angle. The upper blocks are empty, with houses along Wilbur Avenue, the Warren County Hospital in block 346 and a fire department building near Mill Street. The lower blocks, 143 to 147, carry scattered frame dwellings. Adjoining sheets are 17 and 25 above, 28 to the right and 34 below.
notes: Steel is Steele Street in OpenStreetMap.
The detected junctions rest on the grid east of the railroad; South Main Street and Bank Street junctions were not detected.
The grid bends at the diagonal block line below Congress Street, and the fit leaves residuals of 2 to 5 m on both sides of the bend.
100 ft; Wilbur, Hill, Mill, Congress, Bank, Steel (= Steele Street), Kent; Morris Canal

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 shows the eastern edge of the built-up area of Phillipsburg in Lopatcong Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 34 degrees, so that north points toward the upper right. The left two thirds of the sheet is a street grid of long, mostly empty numbered blocks (136, 137, 138, 141, 142, 356 to 360), laid out between Pursel Street at the top, Congress Street across the middle and Kent Street at the bottom, with Gaughran, Gulkin, Green and High Streets running down the sheet. A few frame dwellings and sheds stand along Gaughran and Congress Streets, the I.H. Brensinger School, a pink-coloured brick building with steam heat and electric lights, is at the left edge, and a bottling works stands near Pursel Street. A railroad siding to the Ingersoll-Rand Drill Company curves across the lower centre and cuts the grid. At the right is the Valley View development, a group of houses all coloured blue, with solid concrete walls, floors and roofs and wooden stairs, laid out along Hillside, Arlington, Tuttle, Farm and Hillside Streets and the curving Valley View Circle around a small park, with Stanley Street running south from it. sheet-29-1.description: The main part of sheet 29, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the village of Huntington in Pohatcong Township, east of Phillipsburg, strung along South Main Street. South Main Street crosses the part from the upper left to the lower right, where it turns south and continues as Brunswick Avenue, with Stewartsville Road leaving to the north-east at the turn. North of South Main Street the part shows Dalton Avenue, a street lettered Pohatcong, Hunt Avenue, Center Street (marked not graded) and Shimer Boulevard; to the south Maple Avenue or Pyatts Lane runs off to the south-west and Russell Avenue and Brunswick Avenue run south through thinly built blocks. Pohatcong Creek winds across the left of the part, with a mill race along Dalton Avenue. Most buildings are frame dwellings, with a few stores and an extract factory near the eastern junction. The upper left corner reaches back to Green's Bridge, with Township Road along the Morris Canal, a cement boiler works and vacant hillside. The upper right of the sheet and two boxes along the bottom edge are separate parts drawn on their own: an area north of Alpha, a further stretch of South Main Street and a stretch of Brunswick Avenue with the township school. sheet-30-1.description: The main part of sheet 30, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the west side of the borough of Alpha, south-east of Phillipsburg, as a regular grid of blocks between High (North Av.) at the top and Alpha at the bottom. Cross streets run across the sheet, among them Pursel, Frace, Boulevard North, Bagley, Sampson Avenue, Myrtle, Central Avenue, Argyle, Sigsbee Avenue, Leona, Dewey Avenue and Boulevard South, and they are crossed by Park Avenue along the left edge, Schley Avenue, Pearl, Boulevard East, Helen and Elsie, with Lee Avenue and a multi-track railroad curving down the right side. Most blocks are lined with small frame dwellings numbered along the street fronts, with large blocks near the left edge and the south-west still open. Public buildings include the Alpha Public School, the Magyar Reformed Church, a fire department building and a post office, with a garage and a bakery among the few commercial uses; a passenger station and freight house stand by the railroad at the upper right. A box at the top left is a separate inset drawn on its own, covering High Street and Lee Street at the steel bridge over the railroad. The title cartouche, scale note and compass rose occupy the open top of the sheet, and block numbers 168 to 211 and 373 to 377 mark the lots. Sheet 31 continues the town to the east.
notes: Boulevard North, Boulevard East and Boulevard South are North Boulevard, East Boulevard and South Boulevard in OpenStreetMap; Central Avenue is West Central Avenue.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the east side of the borough of Alpha, beside a multi-track railroad on its left. A grid of numbered avenues, 2nd to 7th, runs from the upper part of the sheet to the bottom, crossed by Warren Avenue, Central Avenue and Euclid Avenue, with Somerset and Joseph across the top and a long strip of Railroad Avenue on the left edge, beside the multi-track railroad. Short alleys, Vine, Apple, Orchard, Firth, Grape and Church, cut the blocks, and the bottom has Sage, Davis and Walters streets running at an angle. The best built part lies between Warren and Central avenues, with a Vulcanite public school, a Hotel Central, a Greek Catholic Russian church and a Hungarian church; the Vulcan Silk Co occupies a long block at the lower left and cement works stand along Church Alley. The upper part of the sheet is a large cemetery and thinly built open blocks crossed by diagonal lines with Brunswick Avenue entering from the top and Joseph lettered across the top right; a street lettered Not Named crosses the bottom. A compass rose, the scale bar and the Phillipsburg title cartouche stand in blank areas. Sheet 30 adjoins on the west and sheet 33 to the south-east.

sheet-34-1.description: The upper part of sheet 34, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and separated from the rest of the sheet by a heavy line, shows the hamlet of Green's Bridge at the south-east edge of Phillipsburg, where South Main Street crosses the Morris Canal and the creek beside it. On the left the Lehigh Valley Railroad, on a steel bridge, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey cross the valley side by side on a diagonal; a cliff runs along their north side. South Main Street runs across the part from left to right below the cliff, with Kent Street branching from it and climbing north-east past Hill Street and Bank Street towards the town; River Road comes up from Carpentersville Road at the lower left and passes under the railroads to meet South Main Street. In the middle the canal and the creek run close together; a head race and tail race serve the Stametz and Pursel feed and flour mill, and a road crosses the canal on a bridge to Township Road, which follows the canal to the north-east towards Huntington on sheet 29. Buildings are few and scattered: frame dwellings along South Main Street and Kent Street, the L.C. Smith bobbin works below the railroad, a hotel at Green's Bridge, a concrete block works by the canal and a public school at the right edge on the line dividing the sheet. A wooded hillside occupies the upper middle of the part.
notes: Placed from two hand-picked junctions only (Hill Street / Kent Street and River Road at South Main Street, which is Carpentersville Road today): a helmert fit, low confidence.
